payload.rationale: Two residuals earned a fix. From s2: `_controller_marker` catches only OSError, so an undecodable `.controller-session` raises UnicodeDecodeError - a ValueError - which escapes the per-run try structure and is swallowed only by main()'s blanket handler, failing open for the WHOLE loop. From s5: the de-fused exclusion sentence now sits after the newly added write-back half and says 'The rule does not apply to wave-raised escalations', so read literally it exempts wave-raised escalations from the escalation-answered write-back as well as from the append. Refactor, then finish the register correction the evidence now supports. THREE things.

(1) THE BLOCK. The violation is real and the threshold stands: nesting_depth 4 exceeds 3 in test_the_per_turn_flag_fact_is_confirmed_with_its_evidence in the new test_doctrine_platform_probes.py. Flatten it - a guard clause, a helper, or a comprehension instead of the nested block - so the assertion set is unchanged and the depth drops to 3 or less. Do NOT weaken, re-tune, or exempt any threshold, and do NOT delete assertions to get under it. 60 of 61 checks already pass; this is the last one.

(2) THE REGISTER CONFLICT IS RESOLVED, IN FAVOUR OF PROMOTION - and your council's own guardrail is what authorises it. That guardrail said: if the shared constraint and platform-probes.md appear to disagree, the code and probe-results.md win. It was right, and on the evidence available it correctly chose Untested. The evidence was incomplete: the controller ran a second probe (B2) before slice s1 was dispatched and never wrote it into probe-results.md. It is now recorded there in full, under the heading 'Probe B2 - does stop_hook_active reset on a NEW user turn? (CONFIRMED)', with the raw four-fire log and a note that it was recorded late. Read it. The result: driving ONE session with TWO user turns via --input-format stream-json, the flag was false at the end of turn 1, true on the continuation, then FALSE AGAIN at the end of turn 2. The third fire is the whole result. Re-run 2026-09-04 and reproduced byte-identically.
